heroHeadline: Resistance Kills 15 Junta Soldiers on Falam-Hakha Road; PDF Destroys Junta Aerial Bomb Convoy in Magway; SAC Drone Strikes Karen Monastery; ASEAN Divided
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,923 of Myanmar's civil war (May 9, 2026), CDF/PDF resistance forces killed 15 junta soldiers in local battles on the strategic Falam-Hakha road in Chin State, demonstrating sustained combat capacity despite the SAC's recapture of Falam (Apr 25-26) and Kennedy Peak (May 7). PDF forces in Seik Phyu Township, Magway Region, ambushed and destroyed a SAC logistics convoy carrying aerial bombs and ammunition — killing 4 soldiers and confiscating weapons — directly degrading junta airstrike resupply capacity in the region. A SAC drone attack on Ledo Township in Karen State (KNU Brigade 3) injured one civilian and destroyed a monastery and two houses, marking the fifth documented monastery attack of 2026. At the 46th ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur, ASEAN remained divided: Thailand proposed direct engagement with Myanmar's foreign minister while Malaysia's chair rejected any softening as 'atrocities continue.' The junta's transfer of Aung San Suu Kyi to house arrest was widely deemed insufficient by the bloc.
footerNote: Data sourced from AAPP, ACLED, UN OCHA, Irrawaddy, RFA, Myanmar Now, DVB, Al Jazeera, Mizzima, Human Rights Watch, Crisis Group, Myanmar Peace Monitor, MoeMaKa CDM News, IMNA / Mon News Agency, CPJ, Narinjara News, Global Arakan Network, Kachin Human Rights Watch, Aryan Age, NUG Ministry of Human Rights, Committee to Protect Journalists, and official NUG, KNU, KIA, AA, and PDF statements.
